MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Agency,
  Community Development Financing Authority,
  Public Improvement Corporation,
  and Library Board of Trustees*

  March 15, 2010

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Agency, the Community
Development Financing Authority, the Public Improvement Corporation, and the Library Board
of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Kelley at 5:01
p.m., on March 15, 2010 at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on March 10, 2010, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Ledesma
  Council Member Schlicht (arrived at 5:03 p.m.)
  Council Member Ury (arrived at 5:30 p.m.)
  Mayor Pro Tem Leckness
  Mayor Kelley

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Irwin B. Bornstein, Assistant City Manager/Director of Admin. Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Pro Tem Leckness

INVOCATION: Mayor Kelley

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Labor Negotiations -- The Council Will Provide Direction to its Labor Negotiator
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6. The Parties to the Negotiations Are

City Council Minutes  1  March 15, 2010
   the City and City's Unrepresented Employees. The City's Negotiator is Dennis
  Wilberg.

CS2. Conference with the City's Real Property Negotiators and Attorney (City Manager
  Dennis Wilberg and City Attorney William P. Curley) Pursuant to Government
  Code Section 54956.8 Concerning the Real Property Known as Turf Lane Park
  Located at 25361 Turf Avenue (APN 619-331-35) in the City of Mission Viejo. The
  Negotiating Parties Are the City of Mission Viejo and the Timberline Community
  Association. Under Negotiation Will Be the Price and Terms of Payment for the
  Potential Sale of the Park to the Timberline Community Association.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:03 p.m., Mayor Kelley recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:11 p.m., with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that for Closed Session Items CS1 and CS2, the Council
gave direction to its negotiators but there was no reportable action.

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Recognize City Volunteers, for their 1,000 Hours of Service

  Mayor Kelley recognized and presented certificates of appreciation to (1) Vera Emerson
  for volunteer hours at the Norman P. Murray Community & Senior Center, (2) Sheryl
  Adams for volunteer hours at the Mission Viejo Animal Shelter, (3) Sheri Lee for
  volunteer hours at the Mission Viejo Animal Shelter, and (4) Stacee Stephan for
  volunteer hours at the Mission Viejo Animal Shelter. Library volunteers Betty Herring
  and Keith Jorgensen were unable to attend the meeting.

P2.  Recognize the Nurses that volunteered to Provide the Flu and H1N1 Vaccinations
  and Blood Pressure Checks at the Norman P. Murray Community and Senior
  Center

  Mayor Kelley recognized and presented certificates of appreciation to (1) Marie Quinter,
  (2) Ruth Dicks, (3) Judy Tuohey, (4) Beverly Butcher, (5) Florence Savage, (6) May
  Hop, (7) Sonia Cartagena, (8) Dolores Crupnick and (9) Anna T. Boyce.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Ross Chun, Aliso Viejo: announced that the 2010 Sustainability Forum will be held in the City
of Aliso Viejo on March 25, 2010, and he invited the City Council Members and staff to attend.

City Council Minutes  2  March 15, 2010
 Christine Saracino, M.V.: expressed concern with the incomplete construction project at 26992
La Paja Lane and complained about generators running all day long. She asked for the status of
the project and requested weekly updates from staff as were done in the past.

Pamela Wheeler, Ms. Senior Orange County 2008, Coto de Caza: invited Mission Viejo women
who are 60 years of age or more (and American citizens) to participate in the Ms. Senior Orange
County Pageant. She stated that this is a very fun event and the top three Orange County
contestants will move to the State pageant in August with the winner going on to compete
nationally.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 10, 15, 16, 17, and 18 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Council Member Ledesma, seconded by Council Member Ury, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said
  titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title
  and further reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the Regular City Council Meeting of March 1, 2010, as
  presented.

3.  Summary of FY 2009-10 Budget Amendments To Date

  Received and filed.

4.  Check Register dated February 19, 2010, in the amount of $1,029,797.20

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Check Register dated February 26, 2010, in the amount of $1,690,800.95

City Council Minutes  3  March 15, 2010
   Ratified the accompanying check register.

6.  General Plan Progress Report for 2009

  Received and filed.

7.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for January 2010

  Received and filed.

8.  Community Development Agency (CDA) Treasurer's Monthly Report for January
  2010

  Received and filed.

9.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer's Monthly Report for January 2010

  Received and filed.

11.  Fiscal Year 2009-10 Budget Amendment for the Mission Viejo Community
  Development Financing Authority (CDFA)

  Adopted CDFA Resolution 2010-02 Amending the FY 2009-10 Budget for the Mission
  Viejo Community Development Financing Authority to Reflect the Issuance of Mission
  Viejo Community Development Financing Authority Lease Revenue Refunding Bonds,
  2009 Series A.

12.  Los Alisos Boulevard Overhead Methacrylate Deck Treatment (CIP 836)

  Approved the bid specifications and authorized staff to advertise for construction bids for
  the subject project.

13.  2009 Residential Slurry Seal (CIP 838)

  (1) Certified the completion of and accepted the improvements for the subject project; (2)
  authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City
  Clerk to record the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the
  faithful performance and payment bonds one year and 35 days, respectively, after the
  date of recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being
  filed with the City; and (4) authorized payment of the final retention 35 days after the
  date of recordation of the Notice of Completion.

14.  2009 Residential Asphalt Overlays (CIP 838)

City Council Minutes  4  March 15, 2010
   (1) Certified the completion of and accepted the improvements for the subject project; (2)
  authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City
  Clerk to record the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the
  faithful performance and payment bonds one year and 35 days, respectively, after the
  date of recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being
  filed with the City; and (4) authorized payment of the final retention 35 days after the
  date of recordation of the Notice of Completion.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

OLD BUSINESS

NEW BUSINESS

19.  City Council Committee Representative Appointments

  Mayor Kelley made new appointments to the regional boards/committees to fill vacancies
  left by former Council Member MacLean. Appoints were made as follows:

  (1) San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency - Mayor Pro Tem Leckness,
  Alternate.

  (2) Measure M Growth Management Area 9 and 10 Interjurisdictional Forum - Mayor
  Pro Tem Leckness, Alternate.

  (3) Orange County Fire Authority Board of Directors - Mayor Pro Tem Leckness,
  Alternate.

  (4) League of California Cities and Orange County Division of the League of California
  Cities - Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, Alternate.

  (5) South Orange County Major Investment Study (SOCMIS) Policy Working Group -
  Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, Alternate.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

10.  Fiscal Year 2009-10 Budget Amendment for the Mission Viejo Community
  Development Agency (CDA)

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Administrative Services Irwin Bornstein presented a
  revised Resolution which properly reflects the borrowing of housing funds.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Ledesma, to adopt
  CDA Resolution 10-02 Amending the FY 2009-10 Budget for the Mission Viejo
  Community Development Agency to Provide for Payment of the Fiscal Year 2009-10

City Council Minutes  5  March 15, 2010
   Mandatory Contribution in the Amount of $1,775,804 to the County Supplemental
  Educational Revenue Augmentation Fund.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

15.  Outdoor Fitness Equipment for Public Use at Oso Viejo Park

  Director of Recreation and Community Services Kelly Doyle presented the staff report.

  Council Member Schlicht expressed concern that plans and design elements were not
  included in the staff report.

  Director Doyle indicated that the plans are on file in the City Clerk’s office and the
  equipment is specifically defined in the bid document and drawings.

  Anna T. Boyce, M.V.: thanked Council Members Schlicht and the entire Council for
  approving the installation of this equipment and stated that the Council will be very proud
  when they see it.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to (1)
  approve the contract bid documents; and (2) authorize staff to advertise for bids to
  purchase and install outdoor fitness equipment at Oso Viejo Park.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

16.  Annual Police Services Motorcycle Maintenance Contract Amendment

  Public Services Administrative Manager Paul Catsimanes presented the staff report.

  Council Member Schlicht inquired about the time frame for the $9,000 addition to the
  contract.

  Mr. Catsimanes responded that it will cover the remainder of the current fiscal year.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to

City Council Minutes  6  March 15, 2010
   approve the First Amendment to the existing contract with Huntington Beach Honda
  Motorcycles to increase the contract from $30,000 to an amount not to exceed $39,000.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

17.  Agreement to Purchase Patron Self-Service Management Tools Software,
  Equipment, and Maintenance for the Mission Viejo Library

  Director of Library Services Valerie Maginnis presented the staff report.

  Council Member Schlicht stated that this is a great service for the community but she is
  concerned that a base bid summary was not included in the staff report and therefore she
  has no idea what constituted the acceptance of the bid. She stated that in the future, she
  would prefer to see bid summaries.

  Director Maginnis responded that the selected vendor presented a very competitive figure
  and provides software compatible with the current integrated library system software.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to (1)
  approve and award the proposed contract with SirsiDynix in an amount not to exceed
  $34,484.56 for automation-related software, hardware, maintenance, and services at the
  Mission Viejo Library, and (2) authorize the City Manager to execute the contract with
  SirsiDynix pending submittal and final review of all required contract documents.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

18.  Oso/Marguerite Intersection Improvements (CIP 844) and Oso Parkway Pavement
  Rehabilitation, Pacific Hills Drive to East City Limit (CIP 205)

  Mayor Kelley announced that she pulled this item from the Consent Calendar to inform
  the public of an improvement that is coming to the residents very soon.

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon presented the staff report and a rough timeline
  for the project.

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS

20.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Mayor Kelley presented the report.

21.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Ury stated that he was unable to attend the recent meeting of the
  Foothill/Eastern TCA.

22.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Kelley announced that she has not attended a meeting since the last report.

23.  SCAG Transportation & Communications Committee (TCC) Report

  Mayor Kelley presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

24.  Update on Solid Waste Facility Tours

  City Manager Wilberg provided an update on the solid waste contract proposals and
  announced that the City’s consultant, Sloan Vazquez, is tentatively offering tours of the
  waste haulers’ facilities on March, 18, 19 and 26 or the week of March 29.

City Council Minutes  9  March 15, 2010
   Mr. Wilberg stated that staff will contact the Council Members to determine their interest
  in attending tours of the waste haulers’ facilities. Should three or more Council Members
  wish to participate in the tours, the City Clerk will call a special meeting in order to
  provide notice to the public via an agenda.

25.  Mid-Year Budget Review for FY 2009-10

  City Manager Wilberg presented the staff report.

  Barbara Anderson, M.V.: inquired about the reserves and the cycle of road maintenance,
  specifically asphalt overlays. She was under the impression that the cycle of repair has
  been extended from five years to seven years.

  The City Council Members asked questions of staff and requested that responses be
  included in the next agenda report.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Kelley, to continue this item
  until the next City Council Meeting.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

City Manager Wilberg discussed Mayor Pro Tem Leckness’ request to look at opportunities for
residents to provide comments related to specific agenda topics. The City Clerk and the
Information Technology Director have done some research and he will forward a memo which
outlines options for the Council’s consideration.

City Attorney’s Report

Following the City Manager’s comments, City Attorney Bill Curley announced that he will
review the options to make sure there are no Brown Act concerns with the proposed concepts for
providing public input on agenda items.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS

26.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as
  presented in the staff report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the
  public record.

City Council Minutes  10  March 15, 2010
 Council Member Ledesma

Council Member Ledesma reminded residents that Bunny Days will be held at the Murray
Community Center on Saturday, April 3, 2010, from 11:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m.

Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht congratulated former Mission Viejo Diablo Perry Webster who helped
the Saddleback College Gauchos win the state basketball title this past weekend. She further
congratulated all of the city’s high school students who have been participating in CIF playoffs
and she stated that they are all champions. Council Member Schlicht announced that she and
Mayor Pro Tem Leckness had a brief discussion about a Town Hall Meeting and she wondered
how the city could go about setting one up. She announced that she is opposed to the use of the
tree logo and she feels that a better representation of the community identity is the city seal.
Council Member Schlicht discussed the number of foreclosures in the last 9 months which
equate to no less than three homes per mile that are in default. She stated that the Council needs
to be respectful of the economic situation and spend the city’s dollars more wisely.

Council Member Ury

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness referred to the earlier discussion of potholes and expressed his own
concern with the health of businesses within the city. He announced that he has recently visited
several companies and auto dealerships and he feels that Mission Viejo’s businesses constitute
the strength of the city. When a business goes out, there is a domino effect and these are the
people we need to take care of. Mayor Pro Tem Leckness recognized that nearby cities have had
auto dealership failures and he stated that the City Council needs to push Mission Viejo
businesses in order to keep them healthy since tax dollars fund other events and services that
benefit the residents. Mayor Pro Tem Leckness announced that the Rotary Club will hold its
annual fundraiser at Café Maiz on Saturday, April 20, 2010, at 6:30 p.m. Proceeds will help
support Rotary service projects within the community so he encouraged residents to attend the
fundraiser.

Mayor Kelley

Mayor Kelley reminded residents that one penny for every dollar spent in Mission Viejo stays in
the city and helps to fund parks, programs and our wonderful facilities. She announced that the
four Mission Viejo Little Leagues had scheduled opening day ceremonies on February 27 and
unfortunately they were rained out. She also announced her attendance at the California Parks
and Recreation Society conference last week in her capacity as an Orange County Parks
Commissioner. She came away with a wealth of information and ideas that she hopes she can
bring to Mission Viejo. Mayor Kelley stated that it was a worthwhile event and she was pleased
to be able to attend the awards ceremony for Mission Viejo’s own Community Services
Commissioner, Ron Ruef who was named Outstanding Commissioner for the State of California

City Council Minutes  11  March 15, 2010
 and who was also elected as President of the California Association of Park and Recreation
Commissioners and Board Members (CAPRBM). Mayor Kelley announced that the Character
Committee youth members will present a Rachel’s Challenge workshop on March 17, 2010, at
7:00 p.m. for elementary school children. Another program, for middle school and high school
participants, will be held on March 24 at 7:00 p.m. at the Community Center. She reminded
residents that Rachel was the first victim of the Columbine shootings and out of her death came
this wonderful program that has touched millions of lives. In Mission Viejo, the Community of
Character is providing local students with strips of paper for writing acts of kindness and the
paper will later form a chain link or chain reaction of kindness. This activity will culminate on
April 25, 2010, at the Arts Alive festival where the links will be connected and stretched for
miles, eventually meeting up with the chain of kindness at Reilly School. Mayor Kelley
encouraged residents to attend Arts Alive on April 24 and 25, 2010, and she reminded residents
that the festival will include the annual Fun With Chalk event. Lastly, Mayor Kelley thanked the
volunteers who were recognized this evening and she announced that the Community of
Character word for the month of March is integrity.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:30 p.m., there being no further business to come before the City Council at this
session, Mayor Kelley adjourned the meeting to Monday, April 5, 2010, at 5:00 p.m.

Karen Hamman, City Clerk
